definitionBean.title: Properties of Acids
definitionBean.definition: Substances that are sour in taste and turn blue litmus paper red are called 'acids'. They produce hydrogen ions ($\text{H}^+$) in aqueous solution[cite: 12].
definitionBean.explanation: Acids are corrosive in nature and liberate hydrogen gas upon reacting with metals[cite: 12]. Their pH value is less than 7[cite: 12].
importantPoints: Produce hydrogen gas on reacting with metals[cite: 12]

definitionBean.title: Properties of Bases
definitionBean.definition: Substances that are bitter in taste, feel soapy to touch, and turn red litmus blue are called 'bases'[cite: 12].
definitionBean.explanation: Bases produce hydroxide ions ($\text{OH}^-$) in aqueous solution[cite: 12]. Bases soluble in water are called 'alkalis'[cite: 12]. Their pH value is greater than 7[cite: 12].

definitionBean.title: Indicators
definitionBean.definition: Substances that change their color or odor in acidic or basic media are called 'indicators'[cite: 12].
definitionBean.explanation: Indicators help identify whether a substance is acidic or basic[cite: 12]. They are of both types: natural (like litmus, turmeric) and synthetic (like phenolphthalein, methyl orange)[cite: 12].
importantPoints: Natural indicators: Litmus, turmeric, red cabbage[cite: 12]
Olfactory indicators: Onion, vanilla, clove oil[cite: 12]

parts.statement: What is an acid? Write any three major physical and chemical properties of acids[cite: 12].
parts.correct_answer: Acids are sour and give H+ ions[cite: 12].
parts.explanation: Acids are substances that are sour in taste and give hydrogen ions ($\text{H}^+$) in aqueous solution[cite: 12]. Major properties: 1. They turn blue litmus paper red[cite: 12]. 2. Their pH value is less than 7[cite: 12]. 3. They react with metals to liberate hydrogen gas[cite: 12].

parts.statement: What is the difference between a strong acid and a weak acid? Give one example of each[cite: 12].
parts.explanation: Acids that ionize completely in aqueous solution to give a large amount of $\text{H}^+$ ions are called strong acids (e.g., $\text{HCl}$)[cite: 12]; whereas those that ionize partially are called weak acids (e.g., $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$)[cite: 12].

parts.statement: Write the major properties of bases and state their effect on litmus paper[cite: 12].
parts.explanation: Properties of bases: 1. They are bitter in taste[cite: 12]. 2. They feel soapy to touch[cite: 12]. 3. Their aqueous solution gives hydroxide ions ($\text{OH}^-$)[cite: 12]. They turn red litmus paper blue and have a pH value greater than 7[cite: 12].

parts.statement: What is the difference between a base and an alkali? Explain[cite: 12].
parts.explanation: Not all bases are soluble in water, but those bases that are completely soluble in water are called 'alkalis'[cite: 12]. Therefore, all alkalis are bases, but all bases are not alkalis[cite: 12].

parts.statement: What are indicators? Give two examples each of natural and synthetic indicators[cite: 12].
parts.explanation: Indicators are substances that show the acidic or basic nature of a solution by a change in their color or odor[cite: 12]. Natural indicators: Litmus and turmeric[cite: 12]. Synthetic indicators: Phenolphthalein and methyl orange[cite: 12].

parts.statement: What are olfactory indicators? Explain with examples[cite: 12].
parts.explanation: Substances whose odor changes in acidic or basic media are called olfactory indicators[cite: 12]. For example, onion juice or vanilla extract, which are used to identify acidic or basic nature[cite: 12].
